The disc, secured with rope, is lifted away to expose the opening, which is described as the "first opening" and dated to six days after an event referred to as "birth" on April 10, 2013.

A person opens a tree cavity to reveal a large, active beehive inside, with bees clustered around the entrance and a dense mass of bees and wax comb filling the interior.

The video opens with a view of a wooden surface, where a small hole reveals a glimpse of activity inside. The camera then zooms in, revealing a dense cluster of bees actively building and tending to a large, intricate honeycomb structure within the cavity. The bees move constantly across the comb’s white wax cells, demonstrating their industrious behavior as they construct and maintain their hive. The entire scene captures the bustling, organized life of a bee colony deep within a wooden structure.

A dense swarm of bees, clustered on a white, textured surface, is shown in close-up, followed by a transition to a large, dark hole in the trunk of a tree. Text overlay identifies this as the "Third Opening," 37 days after the swarm's "birth" on May 11, 2013, indicating the bees have established a new colony within the tree cavity.

The camera zooms in on the dark cavity, then shifts to show a person's hand securing a braided rope across the hole with a metal clip, effectively sealing it.

A hand carefully removes a rope from a tree trunk, revealing a large, circular opening in the wood. The camera then pans inside to show the dark, textured interior of the hollow, revealing small, dark holes and rough surfaces.
A person carefully removes a wooden trap from a tree, revealing a dense swarm of bees clustered inside, showcasing a successful bee collection or relocation effort.

A dense swarm of dark bees clings to the interior wooden walls of a structure, forming a bustling, shifting mass as they actively move and cluster together, indicating a hive relocation or swarming event.

A person carefully removes a honeycomb frame teeming with bees from a hollow tree trunk, revealing the active hive within, before gently placing the frame back into the cavity.

A hand gently probes a dense cluster of bees swarming over honeycomb within a hollow tree, revealing the bustling, living core of the hive.

A person carefully inspects a thriving wild bee colony nestled deep within a hollow tree, their hand gently parting the dense mass of bees to reveal the intricate honeycomb structures and the bustling activity of the hive.
